summary: We created this game project for an audience aged 8 and above. Not only is it entertaining, but it also integrates key facts to educate players on the major events of a planetary landing, specifically on Mars. In our view, creating a simulation like this helps kids better grasp the real dangers of outer space and the importance of being decisive.
details:
Our project is a simulation game built around a core mechanic where players take on the role of an astronaut and complete small, realistic minigames appearing every minute throughout the playthrough. If the player lets the spacecraft's hull integrity drop too low, the game ends and triggers the game-over sequence.

This game helps players expand their knowledge and perspective on the role of an astronaut. Specifically, it educates young players that landing on a planet is not as simple as just flying down; rather, it requires navigating through four distinct stages, from atmospheric/orbital entry to final touchdown.

We aim for the project to have a wide-reaching impact on the youth, especially those interested in space exploration. Through this game, young audiences will gain a deeper understanding of spacecraft landing procedures—particularly the "Seven Minutes of Terror," a critical phase that currently receives little attention among today's youth.

To develop this project, we utilized smart translation tools and consulted AI platforms such as ChatGPT and Gemini for content brainstorming and factual research. Notably, we relied on Claude to assist with coding, debugging, and designing several graphic assets.

The creativity of our project lies in its minigames. They are designed to be accessible and straightforward while remaining grounded in real-world science, presenting players with hypothetical emergencies and specific problem-solving approaches.

Finally, our team carefully considered target demographics, age appropriateness, and the educational value of the content. We prioritized intuitive gameplay and interactive mechanics to ensure the game is engaging, easy to grasp, and appeals to as many young players as possible.
